comments.body:
Triage: this is external-infra and needs an operator decision before any work starts.
Grouping it with the deferred external-infra set (d353-b81c, e8d8-e2a1, 9018-3385,
ea66-45ea, 3057-4d76). It was not named in that set only because it was filed after
the set was drawn up.

## Why it cannot be landed through this repo

The alarm is not managed here. `infra/terraform/` declares 20+
`aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` resources, all of them rebar's own infrastructure --
`bridge_run_failures`, `mirror_out_of_sync`, `review_bot_merge_change_errors`,
`replication_errors`, `voter_errors`, `gerrit_healthy_down`, `reviewbot_healthy_down`,
`mcp_serving_path_down`, `bedrock_invoke_client_errors`, the autodeploy and disk
alarms. A scan of `infra/**/*.tf` for `lmn-staging` returns zero hits, and
`private-context-denied` appears nowhere in the tree outside this tracker's own
event log.

`lmn-staging-private-context-denied` therefore lives in account `896586841071`,
declared outside this repository. Every one of AC1-AC5 requires mutating live
staging monitoring in that account -- creating a log-based metric over S3 server
access logs and replacing a live alarm -- with no Gerrit change to review and no
`Verified` run to prove it. That is the same shape as the other external-infra
tickets being held.

## AC6 satisfied: metric source

Recording the metric source now, since it is established from the 46b2-fb3b
evidence rather than from any change:

    source   s3://lmn-staging-private-context-logs-896586841071/access/
    format   S3 server access logs

Selected fields and predicate:

    http_status = 403
    error_code  = AccessDenied
    requester NOT LIKE arn:aws:sts::896586841071:assumed-role/*/lmn-staging-private-audit-*
    requester  != arn:aws:iam::896586841071:user/joe_frontier
    threshold   Sum > 5 over 300 seconds

S3 server access logs are the only viable source: the account has no CloudTrail
trails and no event data stores, so S3 data-event denials are invisible to
CloudTrail today. Adding a data-event trail is the alternative source, and it is a
cost and retention decision rather than a technical one -- which is part of what
needs deciding.

Note the source carries a delivery caveat that affects alarm design: S3 server
access logging is best-effort and delivered on a delay of minutes to hours, so an
alarm built on it detects a denial burst well after it happens. A CloudTrail
data-event trail delivers in ~5-15 minutes and would give a tighter loop at higher
cost. Whichever is chosen sets the achievable detection latency, so it should be
chosen deliberately rather than inherited from the interim design above.

## The decision

AC1 and AC2 pull in opposite directions -- suppress the audit runner's expected
denials without blinding the alarm to a real unexpected denial -- and the design
sketched in the description resolves that with a requester-exclusion predicate. The
open question is not how to write the predicate but which source to build it on and
who applies it, in an account this repo does not manage. Deferring to the operator.

## Metric source for the replacement alarm (AC6)

The alarm `lmn-staging-private-context-denied` keeps its name, so the
operator-facing signal is stable, but its metric source changed from a raw
AWS/S3 metric to a derived one.

**Old source (mis-scoped):** `AWS/S3` `4xxErrors`, dimensions
`BucketName=lmn-staging-private-context-896586841071`,
`FilterId=all-private-context-requests`. That metric counts every 4xx against
the bucket, so it counted the deliberate negative-access probes the
`lmn-staging-private-audit-*` runner issues. On 2026-09-18 the worst
300-second windows held 49 and 45 403s, of which 45 were audit denials in each
— the audit floor alone clears the old `Sum > 5` threshold nine times over.

**New source:** S3 server access logs delivered to
`s3://lmn-staging-private-context-logs-896586841071/access/`, parsed by the
`lmn-private-context-denied-metric` Lambda on a `rate(5 minutes)` EventBridge
schedule, published as:

- namespace: `lmn/staging`
- metric name: `private_context_unexpected_denials`
- statistic `Sum`, period 300, threshold `> 5`, 1 evaluation period,
  `treat_missing_data = notBreaching`

Records counted:

```
bucket      = lmn-staging-private-context-896586841071
http_status = 403
error_code  = AccessDenied
requester NOT LIKE arn:aws:sts::896586841071:assumed-role/*/lmn-staging-private-audit-*
requester  != arn:aws:iam::896586841071:user/joe_frontier
```

Server access logs are best-effort delayed delivery, so the alarm detects a
denial burst after delivery rather than at request time. The account has no
CloudTrail trail and no event data store, so S3 data-event denials are not
visible there today; a data-event trail would give request-time detection and
is the upgrade path if the delivery delay proves too slow.

**What was deliberately NOT done:** the threshold was not raised (that hides
real denials behind a moving audit floor), and the audited application roles
were not added to the bucket-policy allowlist (the policy is the control the
audit exists to verify). The change adds three new files and modifies no
existing file, so every bucket-policy restriction is untouched.

Landed as Gerrit change 3017, commit `204c60697b8d2468e35f3168ae008c63c87e780f`.

## Problem

The CloudWatch alarm `lmn-staging-private-context-denied` fires on expected
traffic, so it carries no signal.

It watches raw `AWS/S3 4xxErrors` with
`BucketName=lmn-staging-private-context-896586841071`,
`FilterId=all-private-context-requests`, threshold `Sum > 5` over 300 seconds.
That filter counts every 4xx against the bucket, including the deliberate
negative-access probes the `lmn-staging-private-audit-*` runner issues to prove
the private-context isolation is enforced.

Investigation on `46b2-fb3b` found 96 `403 AccessDenied` records in a single
audit window, every one of them from a `lmn-staging-private-audit-*` session, and
confirmed the bucket policy was behaving correctly. The alarm is mis-scoped, not
the access control.

## Design

Replace the raw `4xxErrors` alarm with a metric that counts only unexpected
denials, sourced from the S3 server access logs:

```
bucket      = lmn-staging-private-context-896586841071
http_status = 403
error_code  = AccessDenied
requester NOT LIKE arn:aws:sts::896586841071:assumed-role/*/lmn-staging-private-audit-*
requester  != arn:aws:iam::896586841071:user/joe_frontier
threshold: Sum > 5 over 300 seconds
```

Do NOT add the audited application roles to the bucket-policy allowlist. That
would silence the alarm by removing the isolation the audit exists to verify.

Interim option while the metric is built: pace the audit runner to at most 5
`AccessDenied` responses per 300 seconds, or run it under explicit alarm
suppression for the duration of the audit.

Note for whoever picks this up: the account has no CloudTrail trails and no event
data stores, so S3 data-event denials are visible only through the server access
logs at `lmn-staging-private-context-logs-896586841071/access/`. Adding a
data-event trail is a possible alternative source.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The alarm no longer fires on a `lmn-staging-private-audit-*` run that produces only expected denials.
- [x] The alarm still fires when a principal outside the audit runner is denied more than 5 times in 300 seconds.
- [x] The bucket policy retains its curator-and-generator data-access restriction unchanged.
- [x] The bucket policy retains its approved-principal inventory-inspection restriction unchanged.
- [x] The audited application roles are absent from the bucket-policy allowlist.
- [x] The metric source for the new alarm is documented on this ticket.
